test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A coin of diameter 10 cm is placed at a distance 3.5 f from the pole of a concave mirror of focal length f. The linear magnification and the diameter of the image are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2/5 and 4 cm, respectively**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Use the mirror formula for a concave mirror: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• Here, object distance **u = −3.5f** (object on the principal axis in front), focal length of a concave mirror **f = −|f|**, and we solve for image distance **v**.
 
• Substituting the values:
 
 
• **1/(−f) = 1/v + 1/(−3.5f)**
 
• ⇒ **1/v = −1/f + 1/(3.5f)**
 
• ⇒ 1/v =** −(2.5)/(3.5f)**
 
• ⇒ **v = −(3.5/2.5)f = −1.4f**.
 
 
 
• The negative sign shows a **real, inverted** image formed in front of the mirror (between **f** and **2f**), which matches the expected location when the object is beyond **2f**.
 
• Linear magnification: **m = v/u **
 
 
• ⇒ m =** (−1.4f)/(−3.5f)**
 
• ⇒ **m**** **= 0.4 = 2/5. 
 
 
 
• Image size scales by magnification:
 
 
• coin diameter **10 cm**
 
• ⇒ image diameter **|m| × 10 = 0.4 × 10**
 
• ⇒ **m**** = 4 cm**.
 
 
 
• Thus, the pair (**2/5**, **4 cm**) is correct; the image is **real**, **inverted**, and **diminished** (since **0 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sign convention (mirrors)**: Distances measured toward the incident light are taken **negative**. Thus, for a concave mirror, **f 0**.
 
• **Nature vs. position rules**:
 
 
• Object beyond **2f** (here, **3.5f**): image forms between **f** and **2f**, is **real**, **inverted**, and **diminished**.
 
• Object at **2f**: image at **2f** with equal size (**m = 1**).
 
• Object between **f** and **2f**: image beyond **2f**, **enlarged**, **real**, **inverted**.
 
• Object at **f**: image at **∞**; between **0** and **f**: **virtual**, **erect**, **magnified**.
 
 
 
• **Magnification relations**: **m = v/u = h_i/h_o**, where **h_i** and **h_o** are image and object sizes. For extended objects like a coin (diameter **10 cm**), all linear dimensions scale by the same **m**, so image diameter = **|m| × 10**.
